resources.string: Wait for an unmetered connection before downloading. Downloads requested on mobile data are queued and start on their own once Wi-Fi is back
Queued. Will download when Wi-Fi is available

YouTube has temporarily stopped serving music to this internet connection. It is not your phone, your account or this song, and it clears by itself. Switching to mobile data usually works right away. Otherwise wait a little while and try again.
Puts shuffle, skip, play and repeat together inside one glass bar. Turn it off to have the buttons sit on their own over the artwork. Needs Liquid glass to be on.
YouTube Music suggests these from your account. Your library builds them instead from songs related to what you have played, which works signed out and offline.
Tap to answer, or dismiss with the cross
Your answer is anonymous. All that is sent is which question this was, what you picked, and the app version. No account, no device details, nothing about your library.

InterTune checks for a question now and then and shows it at the top of Home. Off by default. Answers are anonymous: only the question, your choice, and the app version are sent. Nothing is fetched at all while this is off.
Clears the record of what you have answered and dismissed, so past questions can come back.

Every so often InterTune can show a short question at the top of Home, about what to build or change. Answering is optional and anonymous, and you can turn this off at any time in Settings. While it is off, nothing is fetched and nothing is sent.

Catches up every liked song you do not already have. On Wi-Fi only, songs you like while on mobile data are skipped rather than queued, so use this once you are back on Wi-Fi. Songs you deleted by hand will come back.
Paused. YouTube has temporarily stopped serving music to this connection, so downloads are waiting rather than failing. They resume on their own.
You are not on Wi-Fi. Connect to Wi-Fi and try again.
Your liked songs are already downloaded.
Stopped. %1$d downloaded, the rest were cancelled.
Looks up the right volume for songs that are missing it, so nothing suddenly blares out louder than the rest. %1$d songs still need it. Tap to start.
Stopped after several failures in a row, which usually means YouTube wants a break. Fixed %1$d. Try again in a little while.
Done. Fixed %1$d songs, they now play at the same volume as everything else.
Fixed %1$d songs. %2$d have no volume information on YouTube and were left alone.
Looks up the right volume for songs that are missing it, so nothing suddenly blares out louder than the rest. All your songs already have it.
Needs an internet connection to look up song volumes.
Checking song %1$d of %2$d, fixed %3$d so far. Tap to stop.
Stopped. Fixed %1$d songs, the rest are still to do. Tap to resume.
You can change this any time in Settings, under Updates.

InterTune is not on an app store, so it checks GitHub when you open the app and tells you when there is a new version. It can download and install one for you, and Android always asks you to confirm first. You can change this later in Settings.
Higher is more see-through and more strongly refracted; lower is closer to plain solid surfaces
Floating glass panels for the navigation bar, mini player and transport controls, and richer artwork colours behind the now playing screen
Richer artwork colours behind the now playing screen. The floating glass panels need Android 13 or newer
Ease the volume down as the sleep timer runs out, instead of cutting off abruptly
How long the fade out lasts before the sleep timer stops playback
Swiping the mini player downwards closes it and stops the music. Turn this off and it stays put instead, so the song keeps playing and you cannot close it by accident.
Opens the release page so you can read what changed and download it yourself. Useful if the in-app install will not work on this device.
Checks GitHub for a newer version of InterTune each time you open the app. Off by default. Nothing is ever installed without you confirming it.
